title: When successful requests return bad data
scenario: A service can return data with incorrect stock or delivery values. Test how the shop handles these replies.
assignment: Test Wrong or missing values on Lighting inventory and Primary Shipping separately. Keep incorrect values off the page and make missing information clear.

fields.label: Healthy baseline and metric
fields.prompt: Record healthy stock, delivery information and relevant Grafana readings.

fields.label: Hypothesis and fault injection
fields.prompt: Which customer results should remain correct and usable when Inventory or Shipping returns invalid values? What would disprove your hypothesis?

fields.label: Observe the fault’s blast radius
fields.prompt: Compare stock and delivery results with your baseline. Which products and functions are affected? Compare Dependency outcomes with Response checks in Grafana.

fields.label: Mitigation and reason
fields.prompt: Which mitigation did you choose? Why would the other mitigations not solve the problem?

fields.label: Same-fault validation
fields.prompt: Keep the fault and traffic unchanged. Test whether your protection keeps customer results within the limits in your hypothesis. Compare with your baseline and record the evidence.

fields.label: Conclusion and cleanup
fields.prompt: Did you find a weakness? What improved, and what remains limited? Clear faults, restore defaults and verify recovery.

solution: HTTP 200 replies can contain invalid stock, prices or delivery days.
Response checks shows invalid values. Responses rejected counts those blocked when validation is enabled.
Enable Check response data for each service and click its matching Apply settings button. Invalid replies are discarded. The last valid values remain.
Validation does not repair the service or call backup Shipping. Remove faults, restore defaults and verify normal results.

hints.title: Hint 1
hints.explanation: The reply reaches Storefront. Are its values usable?

hints.title: Hint 2
hints.explanation: Packets reaching the storefront does not guarantee correct values. Compare Dependency outcomes with Response checks.

hints.title: Hint 3
hints.explanation: A timeout stops waiting. A breaker pauses failed requests. Neither checks the values in a reply. So maybe we should check if the data is correct.
